# Orch v0.1.1

Starting work now follows the access people were given, invitations and tool connections stay within the authority
that issued them, and environment templates become editable Dockerfiles.

## Update

No manual database or configuration changes are needed. Download the release files for your architecture and run
`./update.sh v0.1.1 --from <directory with the release files>` in the deployment directory; `deploy/README.md`
describes updates and rollback. Unchanged Default and Developer tools templates switch to editable Dockerfile
templates at the first start; each host builds their image the first time an environment needs it.

## Starting work

- **Use of an environment starts threads.** Whoever may use an environment can start a thread in it; Manage is for
  setting the environment up and deciding who uses it.
- **Start threads and Create topics** can be given alone, on a topic and on a project. The middle level of an
  organization, project and topic is now called **Contribute** and includes both; Interact keeps its meaning for
  threads and chats, where it means talking to the agent and people.
- **The environment picker** lists what you can use first. Environments you can see but not use follow under
  **Ask for access**; picking one opens the access request for its Use.
- **The new-thread form** says whether the Directory you type exists in the environment or will be created.
- **Access requests** can ask for a chosen period; one that became unavailable can be asked again.

## Security

- **Invitations stay within their maker's authority:** every invitation's role and permissions are checked against
  what its maker may give, when it is made and again when it is accepted.
- **Tool connections stay with their environment:** a tool connection ticket names the environment and generation it
  was issued for, a resumed connection stays bound to the ticket that opened it, and an agent reaches only the tool
  servers its session was given.

## Turns

- Inputs that have not started survive a lost session during startup; Stop is honoured while a turn is being
  prepared; an interrupted start does not spend a retry attempt; a steer is checked against the running turn's model
  and the sender's current access; an unknown Codex outcome is reported as a failure.

## Environments

- Default and Developer tools are editable Dockerfile templates, built on each host when first needed.
- A full disk while preparing an image is reported as a capacity problem.
- The Local embeddings provider can be added.
- Concurrent discussions and chat edits stay consistent.

## Installation and updates

- Installers report failures (BusyBox `wget`, PowerShell foreground runs), keep proxy settings in the node's service,
  name how to remove only the service, and install the x86-64 connector on Windows on ARM. Updates recover when
  interrupted before a backup, keep the port-signing key readable, and warn before rolling back to an incompatible
  connector minimum.

## Platforms and release

- Connectors and environment hosts are tested on Linux, macOS and Windows; Windows ends process trees by verified
  identity.
- Release packaging fetches every crate it lists in the third-party notices and reuses dependency caches and
  verified native builds; CI runs the whole test suite in shards.
